request.deadline: 12 months from treasury withdrawal, with specific milestones through weeks 6, 12, 16, 18, 24, 52 and quarterly reports at weeks 13, 26, 39, and 52
deliverables: Operations and governance infrastructure including dOSPO team, two advisory councils, legal entity formation, and quarterly reports
Maintenance Fund for high-risk Cardano open source infrastructure using dependency audits, SBOMs, centrality scores, bus factor assessments, retainers, and a public health dashboard
Maintainer Development program building mentor-mentee contributor pipelines
CodeForUs bounty program for targeted delivery work
Ecosystem Activation Reserve funding contributor entry programs
Quarterly public reporting and Mill Law Firm financial review or audit attachments
request.recipient: Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting as funds administrator, with intended later transition target to a dOSPO 501(c)(3) subject to governance.
request.what: Establish a decentralized Open Source Program Office and Open Maintenance Framework to coordinate and sustain Cardano open source infrastructure through four programs over 12 months.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 4,094,000 ADA over 12 months to fund a dOSPO and OMF program for Cardano open source sustainability.
Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting is designated as the sole Article II.7.5 funds administrator from treasury withdrawal through the 12-month period.
Mill Law Firm is designated as independent financial auditor for quarterly cadence through Month 12.
The proposal says advisory councils will publish written feedback before program disbursements, but final allocation authority remains with the designated administrator.

The proposal claims DReps can replace the administrator or shut down the initiative through an on-chain Info Action, and the proposer commits to sponsoring such an action if requested by 15 or more DReps.
The Maintenance Fund would deploy 2,000,000 ADA over 12 months across retainer tiers, with a 175,000 ADA portfolio reserve returned to the treasury if undeployed.
The proposal claims selection will follow published dependency centrality data rather than relationships, using audits, SBOMs, centrality scores, bus factor assessments, and published rubrics.
The proposer claims prior leadership in Cardano open source governance at Intersect and provides website, GitHub, LinkedIn, X, and email references as verifiable history.

The proposal claims dOSPO and OMF whitepapers were developed with experts from Bitergia, CHAOSS, Apache Software Foundation, Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust, Intersect, Andamio Platform, Modus Create, Leadingbit Solutions, and the Chinstrap Community.

The proposal sets KPI targets including 15 or more high-centrality projects funded by Month 12, 40% top-50 dependency coverage, 100% quarterly transparency reporting, and security response time under 48 hours.

summary: The document requests a large 12-month treasury withdrawal for an administrator-led open source sustainability program with governance oversight mechanisms, advisory councils, audits, dependency-based allocation methods, reporting commitments, and several claims of proposer experience and ecosystem alignment.
